chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Thabit ibn Abi Saeed, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about the women who place qaramil (hairpieces/extensions) on their heads. He said: Wool is permissible, and whatever is from the hair of the woman herself [is permissible]. He disliked for the woman to make the qaramil from the hair of someone else. So if she joins her hair with wool or with her own hair, it does not harm her.

key_terms.الْقَرَامِلَ: Hairpieces or extensions worn on the head

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on women using hair extensions made from wool or other people's hair?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguished between the permissibility of hair extensions (qaramil) and the specific dislike (karaha) of using hair from another person, likely to avoid the deception of claiming natural fullness. He permitted the use of wool or the woman's own hair, establishing that joining one's hair with these materials causes no religious harm, reflecting a nuanced approach to female adornment within Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Noman, from Sabit Bin Abu Saeed who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> was asked about the women who were making loops and knots in their heads. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The wool is correct and whatever was from the hair of the woman herself, and it is dislike for the woman that she makes the loops from the hair of someone else. So if she were to join her hair with wool, or with her own hair, so it is not harmful’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Nu’man from Thabit ibn abu Sa‘id who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was asked about women: if they can form their hair in loops and knots.

He (the Imam) said, ‘It can be done from wool or her own hairs and it is Makruh (undesirable) for a woman to form loops and knots on her head from the hairs of other women; but if she joins her own hair with wool it is not harmful.’”
